```{r setup}
library(MolBioR)
```

The package: `MolBioR` allow the user to quickly walk-through the central dogma in R, and includes five functions.

The first function `DNA_seq_generator` creates an arbitrary DNA sequence of a given length:

```{r}
test_DNA <- DNA_seq_generator(90)
test_DNA
```

The second function then takes the `DNA_seq` from the previous function, and transcribes it into RNA. If you want to analyze your own DNA sequence, just input that in the function.

```{r}
RNA_test <- DNAtoRNA(test_DNA)
RNA_test
```

The third function `codon_reader` splits the RNA string into codons. The function has an optional parameter called `start=1`, which determines from which RNA index the open reading frame is set to begin from. It only takes RNA nucleotides, and will raise an error if blank space or other characters is included in the string. The user has to correct this themselves.

```{r}
codon_reader("ABCDE ")
```

```{r}
codon_test <- codon_reader(RNA_test)
codon_test
```

The fourth function: `Translation` takes codons, and translates them into amino acid:

```{r}
aa_test <- Translation(codon_test)
aa_test
```

The fifth and final function `aa_distribution_plot` creates a plot to visualize the distribution of the amino acids in the sequence.

```{r}
pl <- aa_distribution_plot(aa_test)
pl
```
